info.title: groundline
info.description:
groundline checks an AI-written summary, such as a clinical note, against the
source it was written from, such as a consultation transcript. It reports the
facts the summary leaves out (omissions) and the claims in it the source
doesn't support (commissions). It is research code, **not for clinical use**,
and must not be used with real patient data yet.

### Authentication

Both checks need a groundline API key, sent as `Authorization: Bearer gl_...`.
Create one with `groundline-core keys create`, then use **Authorize** below.
`/health` and `/ready` are public.

The body-byte allowance applies to every HTTP path and method, including public
and unknown routes. A declared oversized body can return **413 Content Too Large**
before authentication or **404 Not Found** / **405 Method Not Allowed** responses.
For streamed bodies, the allowance is enforced as the application reads them;
routes that do not read a body do not buffer it to check its size.

### Versions

Both checks are under `/v1`. groundline isn't public yet, so v1 can still
change in ways that break a caller, such as removing or renaming a field. Once
the API is public, v1 will only add: new endpoints, or new fields in a
response. A change that could break a caller, such as removing or renaming a
field or changing a status code, will then get a new prefix, `/v2`. groundline
is still pre-1.0, so it doesn't yet promise how long an old version stays
available after a new one ships. The version next to the title is groundline's
release, not the API version.

See the [README](https://github.com/groundline-dev/groundline#using-the-api)
for more, including what each status means.

post.description:
Find the facts a summary leaves out, and whether to flag it.

Runs the validated all-Opus omission check, which costs about $0.21 for a
typical clinical note. Set the client timeout above the configured
whole-check limit, which defaults to 120 seconds, to allow time for request
and response transfer. Answers 200 for every finished check, flagged or
not.

post.description:
Find the claims a summary makes that its source doesn't support, and
whether to flag it.

Runs a validated commission check (often called hallucination detection),
chosen with `preset`: `commission_quick` by default, or
`commission_reverse_lean`. The `preset` field says what each runs, how it was
measured, what it costs and whether it is confirmed to its pre-registered
standard.
Each preset flags at its own threshold, and both answer in the same shape. A
claim is a commission if the source contradicts it or never mentions it.
Answers 200 for every finished check, flagged or not.

score.title: Score
score.description:
The highest unsupported confidence among the critical commissions; 0 if
there are none.

threshold.title: Threshold
threshold.description: The alarm score at or above which the summary is flagged.

level.title: Level
level.description: The threshold level used, such as strict.

pipeline.title: Pipeline
pipeline.description:
The pipeline that ran. It is a validated preset, whose measured results
apply to this run.

alarm.description:
The alarm score, the threshold it was compared with, and the threshold
level. The summary is flagged when the alarm score reaches the threshold.

usage.description: The model calls the check made, and what they cost.

source.title: Source
source.description: The original material, such as a consultation transcript.

summary.title: Summary
summary.description: The AI-written summary to check, such as a clinical note.

preset.title: Preset
preset.description:
Which validated preset to run.

`commission_quick` (the default): Quick commission check (one Haiku call that lists the unsupported or contradicted claims, refute off, alarm). Measured on 172 held-out commission pairs: 151 caught, 1/110 clean notes flagged, about $0.001 per note. It passed its pre-registered test.

`commission_reverse_lean`: Lean commission check (Opus claims, one Opus support check, Opus refute, alarm). Measured on 172 commission pairs: 166 caught, 0/110 clean notes flagged, about $0.14 per note. It matched the exact preset's catches, but failed both of its pre-registered tests, a paired-score margin less than two pairs wide and a false-alarm limit, so it isn't confirmed to that standard.

examples.source: Doctor: Any allergies? Patient: Penicillin, it gives me a rash. Doctor: Your knee is sprained. Take Motrin 600 mg every 6 hours for a week, and come back if it isn't better in two weeks.
examples.summary: Sprained knee. Allergic to penicillin. Motrin 800 mg every 6 hours for a week. Return if not improving in two weeks.

evaluation_type.title: Evaluation Type
evaluation_type.description: Which check made this response: `omissions` or `commissions`.

flagged.title: Flagged
flagged.description: Whether the alarm score reached the threshold.

score.title: Score
score.description:
From 0 to 1. Higher is better. A score below 0.5 means the summary is
flagged, and a summary passes at 0.5 or above; the flag is exactly the
alarm's. The score is the alarm score turned around and rescaled around the
alarm's threshold. A flag means a claim wasn't found in the source, for
a reviewer to check; the score doesn't say how good the summary is overall.
A summary with no claims the source fails to support scores 1.

findings.title: Findings
findings.description:
The claims in the summary that the source doesn't support, most important
first.

counts.description:
How many of the source's facts the summary records, fully, partly or not at
all. Null for a check that doesn't count facts, such as the commission check.

metadata.description: How the check ran: the pipeline, the alarm behind the flag, and the usage.

findings.statement: Motrin 800 mg every 6 hours for a week

partial.title: Partial
partial.description: Facts the summary only partly records.

Counts.title: Counts
Counts.description: How many of the source's facts the summary records.

ErrorBody.title: ErrorBody
ErrorBody.description: The body of every error but a 422.

type.title: Type
type.description:
`omission`: a fact from the source that the summary leaves out or only
partly records. `commission`: a claim in the summary that the source doesn't
support.

severity.title: Severity
severity.description:
How much it would matter if the fact were left out, or the claim were wrong.
Null when the check didn't grade it.

verdict.title: Verdict
verdict.description:
For an omission, `partial` (the summary records only part of the fact) or
`absent`. For a commission, `unsupported` (the source doesn't mention the
claim) or `contradicted` (the source says otherwise).

confidence.title: Confidence
confidence.description:
From 0 to 1: how sure the check is. For an omission, that the fact is
missing; for a commission, that the source doesn't support the claim. Null
when the check gave none.

statement.title: Statement
statement.description:
The fact from the source that the summary leaves out, or the words in the
summary that make the claim, word for word.

source_evidence.title: Source Evidence
source_evidence.description:
The passage of the source behind the finding. For an omission, the passage
the fact came from. For a contradicted commission, the passage the model quoted
as contradicting the claim. Null for an unsupported commission, or if the model
quoted none.

summary_evidence.title: Summary Evidence
summary_evidence.description:
For a partial omission, the words in the summary that partly record the
fact. Null otherwise.

evidence_found.title: Evidence Found
evidence_found.description:
Whether `source_evidence` appears in the source word for word, ignoring
case, punctuation and spacing. True means verified. False only means it
couldn't be matched, which a reworded quote or markup in the source, such as a
scribe's tags, can cause; it doesn't mean the passage was invented. Null when
there is no evidence.

explanation.title: Explanation
explanation.description:
What kind of problem this is, in a fixed sentence for each type and verdict.
It is the same for every finding of that kind, so use the other fields for the
details.

Finding.title: Finding
Finding.description:
One omission or one commission, as a check reports it. The same fields serve
both kinds, so a check that finds both can return them in one list.

score.title: Score
score.description:
The highest missing confidence among critical facts still flagged, with
partials at half weight; 0 if there are none.

threshold.title: Threshold
threshold.description: The alarm score at or above which the summary is flagged.

level.title: Level
level.description: The threshold level used, such as strict.

pipeline.title: Pipeline
pipeline.description:
The pipeline that ran. It is a validated preset, whose measured results
apply to this run.

alarm.description:
The alarm score, the threshold it was compared with, and the threshold
level. The summary is flagged when the alarm score reaches the threshold.

usage.description: The model calls the check made, and what they cost.
